Hi Asha / Kyle —

Thanks again for the time today. Wanted to capture the main takeaways and proposed next steps so we have a mutual action plan to keep momentum on the pilot. Key items we covered: 

- Procurement path: primary preference is PO (finance-led). Card payment is acceptable for initial POC if procurement can approve a low-dollar pilot, but PO is the expected path for production.
- Legal/security: Skyline will run a quick legal review of our MPA + standard security questionnaire; security will validate data residency and audit log requirements.
- Timeline: you estimated ~2 weeks for legal, ~1-2 weeks for security, and finance/PO issuance potentially 1-3 weeks after approvals depending on procurement backlog.
- Marketplace: you asked about third-party marketplace (AWS Marketplace) — you are open to it but procurement prefers direct PO for contracting simplicity.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I will send an updated MPA draft with our standard security addendum (attached).
2) Asha / Kyle to confirm the internal owners for legal, security, and finance and provide approximate SLAs.
3) We schedule a short MAP check-in next Wednesday to review progress and unblock items.

Attachments: Redwood_MPA_Draft_v2.docx, Redwood_SOW_Template.pdf (see attached stubs).

If that captures it, can you confirm owners and whether procurement would accept a short POC on card while the PO is processing?

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our discussion. Quick updates from our side: 

- Legal: assigned to Priya Mehta (legal). She'll do an initial pass on your MPA and expects to flag non-standard clauses within ~10 business days.
- Security: our security team (lead: Kevin Liu) will run through the questionnaire. They typically take 1-2 weeks for cloud vendors with standard addendums. They will focus on audit logs, encryption at rest, and network isolation for any private deploys.

Hi Asha / Kyle —

Thanks for the updates and for lining up the internal owners. A couple quick clarifications from the commercial side: 

- POC options: we can support a short evaluation on card for up to $5k. The POC on card lets you validate integration faster while procurement and legal run the PO track.
- Marketplace: purchasing via AWS Marketplace can simplify billing for procurement teams that prefer it, but it does not replace the need for legal/security review if you require specific data residency or private deployment constraints. In many cases procurement still requests a PO for larger/prod purchases even if the license is available on marketplace.
- Pricing: for the POC we can offer a trial discount (15%) for the first month. For annual PO-based commitments we will provide standard volume discounts depending on committed spend.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Marissa to upload the finalized MPA to the shared Drive and loop in Priya and Kevin.
2) If procurement agrees to the card POC, we can get a credit card invoice issued within 48 hours after purchase.
3) If procurement prefers PO, procurement@skylinehealth.com to share their PO template and expected turnaround.

If that sounds good, Asha — please confirm which route you'd prefer for the initial evaluation and whether we should start the POC while legal runs the MPA. Happy to jump on the MAP check-in next Wednesday to sync.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
